calls.head: The Capitals give up good looks, and the Lightning take them
calls.body: The Capitals have struggled to prevent dangerous shots, and the Lightning don’t waste many.
calls.call: The Lightning’s average shot has at least their usual 6.5% chance of going in.
calls.nums: Tampa Bay 7th for shot quality (a 6.5% chance of scoring on the average shot) · Washington 24th for preventing dangerous shots
calls.cite: Style fingerprint · this season blended with last · 1 and 1 games this season
calls.happened: Tampa Bay’s average shot had a 6.7% chance of going in, against their usual 6.5%.

calls.head: The Lightning hound the puck; the Capitals sit back
calls.body: On forecheck pressure, Tampa Bay is near the top of the league and Washington is one of the league’s worst. That’s about as far apart as two teams get.
calls.call: The Lightning put more forecheck pressure on than the Capitals.
calls.cite: Style fingerprint · this season blended with last · 1 and 1 games this season
calls.happened: On forecheck score (arena-adjusted, 100 is league average), Tampa Bay had forecheck score 139 and Washington forecheck score 92. Coming in, Tampa Bay was at forecheck score 103 and Washington at forecheck score 85.

TBL.head: We gave Tampa Bay a 70% chance, and Tampa Bay delivered.

WSH.head: We gave Washington only a 30% chance, and it went the way we feared.

surprises.head: Washington couldn’t get good looks
surprises.body: Washington’s shots at 5-on-5 were less dangerous than usual: a 4.4% chance of scoring on the average shot, against their usual 6.7% (league average 6.3%). A team strays this far about once every 40 games.

surprises.head: Tampa Bay tried a different line
surprises.body: B. Point, G. Goncalves, N. Kucherov played 9:58 together at 5-on-5, a trio that isn’t one of Tampa Bay’s usual lines.

story.head: The Lightning beat the Capitals
paras: Charle-Edouard D'Astous opened the scoring early in the first. Conor Geekie scored the winner late in the first.
The chances were close to even, so this one could have gone either way. The Lightning tried a line they hadn’t used before: Brayden Point, Gage Goncalves and Nikita Kucherov.

items.text: Whether the Lightning keep that line together at home against Philadelphia on Monday.
Both of the preview’s calls held.
